title: Console walkthrough - usage analytics & per-route cost breakdown
summary: Redwood AE + SE walked BetaHealth through the Console usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and token-level cost breakdown. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated for a HIPAA-adjacent workload, wants end-to-end cost visibility and audit trails. Agreed to run a 2-week pilot with sample traffic and an initial benchmark; Redwood to provide pricing, security pack, and pilot runbook.
next_steps: Sofia to share pilot runbook and pricing sheet by 2026-07-10
Daniel to schedule benchmark run and provide sample payloads by 2026-07-12
BetaHealth (Aisha) to provide representative traffic patterns and 3 example routes by 2026-07-11
Leah to request SOC2 + encryption docs; Redwood to attach security pack in email

Daniel Cho: Prepare benchmark template and sample payloads; coordinate test window - due 2026-07-12
Aisha Khan: Share traffic patterns and top 3 routes for cost analysis - due 2026-07-11

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-08
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Daniel Cho (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (BetaHealth - Head of MLOps), Dr. Miguel Santos (BetaHealth - CTO), Leah Park (Compliance), Ravi Patel (Infra)

[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Sofia from Redwood, AE on the account, and with me is Daniel, our SE.
[00:12] Daniel: Hi all, good to meet you. We'll do a 30-ish minute console walkthrough focused on usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and how cost breaks down at token level; then leave time for Q&A and next steps.
[00:26] Aisha: Sounds good, we have about 50 minutes so that works. Quick context: we're evaluating a couple of vendors for hallucination-sensitive features in our patient triage flow. HIPAA-adjacent, so compliance is a big factor.
[00:43] Leah: Yes, compliance first. We need audit logs, SSO/SAML, KMS integration, RBAC, encryption/KMS, data residency options, and clarity on retention.
[00:54] Sofia: Absolutely, we'll hit the compliance pieces and I'll attach the security pack. Quick question on scale - what are you seeing today in terms of routes and qps?
[01:05] Aisha: Right now it's 3 main routes in prod (triage, summarization, intent classification), peaks around 120 qps, average payloads about 300 tokens in/350 tokens out. We're planning to increase to 300 qps over next quarter.
[01:20] Daniel: Great, that gives us a baseline. We'll show how per-route dashboards surface cost per route and token usage breakdown so you can map that directly to product features.
[01:33] Sofia: Starting the console - apologies if screen blips out, connection is a bit laggy.
[01:40] Daniel: (screen share) Ok, this is the Redwood Console home. Top-level usage chart shows overall token consumption and average latency. You can filter by model, deployment type (hosted vs dedicated), and time range.
[01:58] [01:58] Daniel: Here is the per-route dashboard - we auto-ingest route tags from the API and show token counts, cost, p50/p95 latency, error rate, and payload histograms.
[02:12] Aisha: Quick nit - can you split by environment, e.g., prod vs staging?
[02:16] Daniel: Yes, environment is a first-class filter; you can also annotate deployments so a canary shows separately.
[02:24] [02:24] Daniel: On the right, cost breakdown. This is token-level cost attribution: model cost, infra surcharge for dedicated pools, and any caching savings applied. You can see dollars per 1k tokens per route.
[02:40] Sofia: We also surface batching impact - toggles show what batching/config suggestions do to per-token cost.
[02:52] Aisha: How accurate is that cost estimate? We need it to map to our finance reports.
[02:57] Daniel: It's driven by run-time telemetry and current pricing profiles. For hosted it's per-token rate; for dedicated there's a reserved capacity amortization plus per-token model cost. Estimates are within ~5-10% of billed for normal traffic patterns; for bursty workloads we recommend a small calibration run.
[03:18] Ravi: On dedicated amortization - can we see the math? We'd want to show ops and finance teams.
[03:24] Daniel: Yup, the console exposes a cost model breakdown. You can export a csv with per-route line items. It includes reserved GPU cost allocation, model quantization adjustments, and batching/caching-derived savings.
[03:37] [03:37] Daniel: Example: triage route is high output tokens due to long summaries, so it's about 60% of total spend even if throughput is only 30% of qps. Summarization is the big one.
[03:50] Aisha: That matches our expectation. So if we optimize summarization model quantization or prompt engineering, we should see big savings.
[03:58] Daniel: Exactly - the console also surfaces recommendation flags: suggest quantization profile (like int8 or 4-bit), or suggest prefix caching for repeated context.
[04:10] Leah: On caching - any data residency concerns? We can't cache PHI outside our iso region.
[04:16] Daniel: Good call. For Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments, cache remains customer-controlled. For hosted we offer region controls and you can disable caching per-route. We'll also log cache hits without storing PHI in the shared cache.
[04:30] Sofia: We had a customer mix up earlier with KV cache naming - sometimes leak of identifiers in the transcript, but we keep the data protections in the docs. I'll include the caching controls section in the security pack.
[04:45] Aisha: What about SSO and access controls for the console and API keys? We need RBAC and SAML.
[04:51] Daniel: Console supports SAML 2.0 SSO, SCIM provisioning, and fine-grained RBAC. API keys are auditable and tied to tokens; you can restrict keys to routes and IP allowlists.
[05:05] [05:05] Daniel: Moving to per-route drilldown: clicking triage route shows per-model usage, average input/output token, latency distribution, and cost per 1k tokens. There's also an anomalies tab for sudden token spikes.
[05:22] Aisha: Do you provide cost allocation tags so we can push to our billing system?
[05:26] Daniel: Yes, you can attach internal tags and export mapping for your finance tools. We also provide an API to pull cost reports programmatically.
[05:36] [05:36] Dr. Miguel: A couple security questions - KMS integration and HSM support?
[05:42] Daniel: We integrate with major KMS providers (AWS KMS, Google KMS) and support customer-managed keys for Private deployments. For Hosted we offer envelope encryption with customer-managed keys. HSM direct integration is part of the Private package.
[05:58] Leah: SOC2 type II report?
[06:02] Sofia: We have SOC2 and ISO documentation; I'll link those in the follow-up email.
[06:10] [06:10] Daniel: Back to cost controls - here's the Optimize panel: suggestions for batching size, cache TTLs, and model alternatives. It can simulate cost for hypothetical changes, e.g., quantize model A to int8 reduces cost by ~22% for your summarization route in the sample.
[06:30] Aisha: That simulation is useful. How do we validate quality/regressions after quantization? We can't degrade triage accuracy.
[06:36] Daniel: We integrate with evals: you can run a prompt set before/after quantization and get quality deltas. The console highlights regressions beyond configured thresholds and can auto-roll back to a fallback model.
[06:52] [06:52] Ravi: For the benchmark, what's the recommended test harness?
[06:56] Daniel: We'll provide a benchmark runbook - it includes concurrent qps targets, representative payloads, and scripts to collect p50/p95/p99 latency plus token counts. We'll sync on a test window.
[07:08] [07:08] Sofia: Quick note - BetaHealth mentioned earlier they have peaks at 120 qps. For an initial pilot we recommend a 2-week dedicated pilot on a small reserved pool to validate latencies and cost.
[07:20] Aisha: 2 weeks seems reasonable. We'd like to include our compliance folks in the pilot access.
[07:26] Leah: Yes, we'll need audit logs and SSO during pilot.
[07:30] Daniel: We'll enable SSO and scoped RBAC for pilot seats. Audit logs can be shipped to your SIEM or downloaded from the console.
[07:42] [07:42] Daniel: Now showing a cost anomaly example - you can set alerts on token spend thresholds per-route and get Slack/email notifications.
[07:52] Sofia: Also, routing policies - you can route to a cheaper model for non-critical routes or to a higher-SLA one for triage. That shows up in the per-route config.
[08:05] Aisha: What about fallback if a dedicated pool is saturated? We can't have triage failed.
[08:10] Daniel: We support smart routing and automatic fallback to hosted compatible variants. You can set per-route policies to failover to a lower-latency or higher-cost route depending on priorities.
[08:22] [08:22] Dr. Miguel: We're also assessing latency SLOs - what p95 can you guarantee on dedicated?
[08:28] Daniel: SLA varies by pool size and model; typical p95 for a 4-GPU dedicated pool on smaller models is sub-200ms; for larger context or heavy models it's higher. We can put numbers against your payloads in the benchmark.
[08:42] Aisha: Can we run an A/B where 50% goes to quantized model and 50% to baseline to measure quality?
[08:48] Daniel: Absolutely - console supports canary/A-B routing and automatic traffic split. It captures metrics per variant and can auto-fallback on regression.
[08:58] Sofia: Small callout - we sometimes see transcription name confusions: Redwood Console used to be called Redwood Console - all the same product.
[09:06] Sofia: (laughs) yes, apologies.
[09:10] [09:10] Daniel: Jumping to exports - here's the csv export. You can get per-route, per-day lines with token counts, model, cost, and annotations. Useful for finance and apportioned billing.
[09:26] Aisha: Can that integrate into our internal billing pipeline? We use Snowflake and CostCenter tags.
[09:32] Daniel: We have a Snowflake-friendly export and S3 dump option. You can push to your warehouse nightly.
[09:40] [09:40] Ravi: Any example customers in health who did this?
[09:44] Sofia: We have a healthcare customer (anonymized) who reduced summarization cost by 28% after applying quantization + prefix caching recommended by Optimize; they kept quality within 1% measured on their eval set.
[09:58] Leah: Interesting - we'll want that case study if possible.
[10:02] Sofia: We'll share an anonymized deck.
[10:06] [10:06] Daniel: Quick demo of latency trace - clicking a request shows the routing path, GPU time vs queuing, and whether prefix cache hit occurred. This helps identify where to optimize.
[10:20] Aisha: That's helpful for debugging token surges.
[10:24] [10:24] Daniel: A couple implementation notes: for dedicated you reserve nodes and can configure autoscale and burst capacity. For short spikes, burst buckets can absorb traffic.
[10:36] Ravi: Autoscale config - do we pay for standing idle GPU capacity?
[10:40] Daniel: Reserved capacity is billed as a monthly commitment. Autoscale can add transient capacity billed at a higher rate. The console models both so you can see amortized and on-demand costs.
[10:54] [10:54] Aisha: Regarding data retention, we need logs retained for 7 years for some audit reasons. Can you commit to that?
[11:00] Leah: Also log access controls.
[11:04] Daniel: We can retain audit logs per contract and ship to your storage. For the console-level logs we provide retention settings; for raw payloads we recommend Private deployment if retention is long-term.
[11:18] [11:18] Sofia: We're at the halfway mark; any burning questions before we go deeper on the pilot plan?
[11:26] Aisha: One: can we preview the security pack?
[11:29] Sofia: Yes, I'll attach SOC2 report, KMS guide, and Private deployment checklist.
[11:35] Leah: Two: encryption-at-rest keys - if we use envelope encryption, where are master keys stored?
[11:40] Daniel: Customer-managed keys live in your KMS; Redwood never persists the master key. For Private we can use HSM.
[11:50] [11:50] Daniel: Back to pilot - proposed scope: 2-week dedicated pilot, triage+summarization routes only, SSO enabled, audit logging to BetaHealth SIEM, and a benchmark run during week 1.
[12:04] Aisha: What's the expected cost for pilot? We need an estimate to approve quickly.
[12:09] Sofia: We'll provide a pilot pricing option - often a modest reserved pool discount for pilot customers. I'll include two options in the sheet: minimal reserved for latency guarantees and a fully-hosted trial.
[12:24] [12:24] Dr. Miguel: For the benchmark, we want to measure p95 and quality delta post-quantization. Can you run the evals automatically?
[12:30] Daniel: Yes - we can run customer-supplied eval sets through both baseline and quantized variants and surface diffs.
[12:38] Aisha: Ok great. Next, are there logs of prompt history for explainability?
[12:44] Daniel: We store prompt metadata and can persist redacted prompts depending on your policy. For PHI we recommend redaction or using Private.
[12:55] Sofia: Quick aside - sometimes product names get mis-typed in notes, e.g., KV cache vs K-V cache, but the functionality is stable.
[13:02] Aisha: Understood.
[13:06] [13:06] Daniel: We'll run through a quick scenario: show how a sudden spike in summarization tokens would be alerted and how to roll traffic to a fallback. (demo)
[13:22] Aisha: Nice. Can alerts push to Slack and PagerDuty?
[13:27] Daniel: Slack, email, webhook; PagerDuty via webhook integration.
[13:34] [13:34] Ravi: What's the SLA for alert delivery?
[13:38] Daniel: Delivery is near-real-time; alerting reliability is part of SLA for Dedicated. We'll put details in the contract.
[13:48] [13:48] Sofia: Ok, let's walk through the proposed next steps and owners.
[13:54] Sofia: Sofia will send pricing + security pack; Daniel will prepare benchmark runbook and sample payloads; BetaHealth to send traffic patterns and eval prompts.
[14:06] Aisha: We'll try to get the traffic patterns and evals to you by Friday.
[14:12] Leah: We'll consolidate compliance questions and send them as a single doc.
[14:16] [14:16] Daniel: Any final questions on routing policies or cost attribution?
[14:20] Dr. Miguel: None from me. This looked thorough.
[14:24] Aisha: One last question - are there discounts for multi-quarter reserved capacity?
[14:29] Sofia: Yes, standard multi-quarter reserved pricing applies; I'll include term options in the pricing sheet.
[14:36] [14:36] Sofia: Ok wrapping up - we'll follow up with an email that contains: pilot runbook, pricing sheet, SOC2/ISO docs, and the benchmark template.
[14:46] Daniel: And I'll schedule the benchmark kickoff once BetaHealth shares evals and traffic patterns.
[14:52] Aisha: Great, thanks both.
[14:56] Sofia: Thank you, everyone.
[15:00] End of recording.

Notes: Transcript has occasional mis-attributions and typos; names may be spelled differently in the console.
